title: Verify GRAPH-scoped zero-length path */? over named graphs
description:
property-paths-design flags the one likely-latent bug: for a path inside GRAPH ?g { ... }, the reflexive (zero-length */?) domain must be THAT graph's nodes, but eval_path's view::default_is_empty() gating (exec.rs:1993) plus the constant-intern path are subtle and the W3C suite (default-graph only) does not cover it. Add a hand-written test: SELECT * WHERE { GRAPH ?g { ?x :p* ?y } } over two named graphs with disjoint node sets, asserting each graph's zero-length domain is its own nodes. Acceptance: the test passes (or, if it fails, fix eval_path so GRAPH-scoped zero-length ranges over the active graph's nodes).

title: Core: cheap O(overlay) Graph::snapshot API (Arc-shared base)
description:
Graph is not cheaply cloneable (deep-copies the dict arena + six permutations, O(n)), forcing the server's update path to double-buffer and blocking sparq-rsp's true-overlay eval (item 3), sparq-py's Graph.copy(), and the RDF/JS incremental-update story. Add Graph::snapshot(&self)->GraphSnapshot: O(overlay) (never O(triples)), immutable + Send+Sync, unaffected by later update_in_place/compact (new base into fresh Arcs). Requires moving TripleStore::perms + the compacted dict arena behind Arcs across every storage mode (mmap + compressed). Acceptance: the three blocked consumers unblock; server Writer collapses to one master + per-commit Arc::new(snapshot()).

title: HDT: sparq-side direct SPO decoder skipping TriplesBitmap::new
description:
HDT loads at 416k triples/s, ~12x below the NT fast path, because upstream Hdt::read builds a full WaveletMatrix + OP-index + rank/select that sparq's one-shot SPO scan never queries. Reimplement just the triples-section read in sparq-hdt: read bitmap_y/z + sequence_y/z and iterate SPO directly (predicates from sequence_y, not the wavelet), stopping before TriplesBitmap::new. Acceptance: identical BTreeSet<[String;3]> vs graph_from_hdt(Hdt::read(...)) on the same bytes (incl. multi-block-PFC + shared-section fixtures), with the index-build stage gone from per-stage timing.

title: HDT: PFC block-sequential dict decode + borrowed-slice interning
description:
Each upstream extract(id) re-walks the PFC block from its start (~8 redundant vbyte-delta steps) and allocs a fresh Vec<u8>+String per id, though sparq materializes every id in each section exactly once. Walk each PFC section block-by-block decoding the whole block once into a reusable buffer (O(N) not O(N·block_size)), then intern from borrowed &str/&[u8] slices instead of the String round-trip. Acceptance: dict-decode stage time down, differential BTreeSet equality across block boundaries, reduced alloc count.

title: ZK: enforce globally-unique per-graph salts at trusted ingest
description:
Audit #9: the cross-graph bnode 'distinct by construction' guarantee rests on distinct per-graph salts, but salt never enters any circuit, the verifier never compares salts, registry.rs accepts any caller salt with no uniqueness check, and salt_from_bytes is test-only (no OS-random ingest path). A salt-reusing ingester correlates bnodes across graphs. Acceptance: draw 32 OS-random bytes per graph at registry mint, bind the salt under the issuer signature so reuse is detectable, or bind salt into the in-circuit attribution check.

title: MPC: replace SplitMix64 sim RNG with a CSPRNG for masking
description:
The Shamir backend's in-process simulation uses a deterministic SplitMix64 for the dealer's masking coefficients (flagged in shamir.rs, not hidden). Production needs a cryptographically secure RNG for the masking so privacy holds against a real adversary. Acceptance: dealer masking draws from an OS-seeded CSPRNG, gated so tests can still pin determinism; documented in shamir.rs.

Uniform F_p via 61-bit-mask + rejection (no modulo bias). clippy -D warnings clean; 40 mpc tests green. Commits 2e71077, 7beea04.

title: MPC: linear cuckoo-bin oblivious hidden-value join (Q3/RQ2b)

title: Vectors: persistent on-disk ANN index (DiskANN/Vamana)
description:
The sparq-vectors HNSW index is rebuilt from the mmap'd store on every open (~33s for 50k×32 release on M1); for 10M+ vector stores the index itself should be a versioned on-disk artifact — a DiskANN/Vamana-style graph with mmap'd adjacency (or instant-distance serde persistence as a stopgap). Acceptance: a versioned on-disk ANN artifact opened without a full rebuild, with recall parity to the rebuilt index.

Source: crates/sparq-vectors/TODO.md#persistent-ann
Notes: Source: sparq-vectors/TODO.md 'Persistent / out-of-core ANN DEFERRED'. Adds serde+bincode + a second format to version; deferred until a workload hits the rebuild wall.

title: Vectors: scalar/product quantization for 100M-scale stores
description:
sparq-vectors is f32-only; scalar i8 (4x) or product quantization is needed for 100M-scale stores. The .spqv header has 12 reserved bytes for an encoding tag so it lands as a backwards-compatible header bump. Acceptance: an i8/PQ-quantized .spqv variant readable by existing open paths with a documented recall/size tradeoff.

Source: crates/sparq-vectors/TODO.md#quantization
Notes: Source: sparq-vectors/TODO.md 'Quantization DEFERRED'. Header reserved bytes already allocated; deferred until a driving workload + recall budget exist.

title: CI: flip the fmt+clippy gate from informational to hard
description:
The ci.yml fmt+clippy job runs cargo fmt --all --check + clippy informationally (the codebase predates a rustfmt.toml). Add a rustfmt.toml, run cargo fmt --all to reformat the tree, then flip the gate to hard-fail. Acceptance: cargo fmt --all --check passes on main and the CI job is a required gate (no longer 'informational').

Source: .github/workflows/ci.yml#fmt
Notes: Source: ci.yml:51-60 ('clippy run informationally for now ... tightened in a later [pass]'). The reformat is the prerequisite within this same task.

title: RSP-QL: surface syntax parser + multi-window joins
description:
sparq-rsp's register takes plain SPARQL + a programmatic WindowSpec; there is no RSP-QL text parser (FROM NAMED WINDOW :w ON STREAM :s [RANGE PT10S STEP PT5S]) and no named streams / multiple windows per query. Implement the RSP-QL surface syntax + multi-window-join support (each window its own S2R state, the engine a dataset-per-window view). Acceptance: an RSP-QL query string with >=2 named windows registers and evaluates equal to the programmatic equivalent.

Source: crates/sparq-rsp/TODO.md#rsp-ql-syntax
Notes: Source: sparq-rsp/TODO.md 'RSP-QL surface syntax DEFERRED'. A parser + multi-window-join design; revisit when a consumer speaks RSP-QL text.

title: Retire vendor/spargebra once the upstream release lands
description:
Crates.io builds resolve upstream spargebra 0.4.6, so the vendored SPARQL-parser conformance fixes (vendor/spargebra/SPARQ-PATCHES.md) apply only to git builds until the upstream PRs land. Watch for the next spargebra crates.io release carrying the fixes, then drop the vendored copy and re-point the workspace at the published crate. Acceptance: vendor/spargebra removed, workspace depends on the published spargebra, conformance unchanged (still >=1229).

title: wasm+JS: streaming/cursor query result API
description:
Store.query returns one JSON string, double-buffering large results (wasm string + JS parse), so the JS layer can only expose a materialised array, not an RDF/JS ResultStream. The engine half landed (query_json_chunks_with_budget returns ordered chunks). Add the wasm export over it (e.g. query_page(sparql, offset, limit) or a per-row callback) so JS can expose a true streaming ResultStream<Bindings> with bounded memory. Acceptance: queryBindings() returns a ResultStream backed by the chunked/cursor wasm export.

Source: js/TODO.md#streaming-cursor
Notes: Sources: js/TODO.md streaming + StringSparqlQueryable follow-up. Engine half (query_json_chunks_with_budget) done; wasm export remains.

title: wasm: CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE export for queryQuads()
description:
Engine construct/describe + construct_ntriples* landed (T16), but there is no wasm export, so the JS queryQuads() cannot reach CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE. Add an additive wasm export (e.g. Store.construct(sparql)->string returning N-Triples) so the JS layer can parse it. Acceptance: queryQuads() over a CONSTRUCT query returns the constructed quads via the new wasm export.

title: Engine: native budgeted ASK / exists() early-exit
description:
sparq_engine has ask_prepared, but the JS/RDF-JS layer's path and any consumer wanting a budgeted boolean still benefit from a true early-exiting exists(). Confirm/extend native ASK so it stops at the first solution rather than computing a full count, and expose it through wasm. Acceptance: ASK over a large match set returns after the first solution; a wasm export wires it to the JS layer (which currently rewrites ASK->SELECT * and counts).

title: Engine: planner pushdown hook for geof: filter -> GeoIndex window
description:
The geo registry evaluates geof: functions post-hoc (per row, after pattern matching). Pushing geof: spatial filters down into a GeoIndex window query (the performant plan) needs a new planner rewrite hook in sparq-engine where a registered predicate+filter shape claims a scan — distinct from the cs-planner statistics seam (which is a statistics injection, not a physical-operator substitution). Acceptance: a registered geof: distance/intersects FILTER is substituted by an index window scan, validated equal to the post-hoc result.

Source: crates/sparq-geo/TODO.md#planner-pushdown
Notes: Source: sparq-geo/TODO.md 'Deferred: planner pushdown'. A physical-operator substitution rewrite hook; the cs-planner estimator seam does not cover it.

title: Turtle: memchr/SIMD the statement-terminator pre-scan
description:
next_terminator (lib.rs:2341) is a scalar byte loop with no memchr/SIMD; the pre-scan walks the entire body once before fan-out, pure critical-path latency. Replace the inner advance-to-next-interesting-byte with memchr3(b'.', b'<', b'"', ...) behind the parallel feature. Acceptance: pre-scan stage time down, all existing Turtle differential tests still pass.

Source: research/parsing-optimization-plan.md#T2
Notes: Source: parsing-optimization-plan.md Turtle T2 (Wave B3). Honest: small win (scanning is ~0.4% of bandwidth); do it because cheap+low-risk.

title: Turtle: per-chunk prefix-snapshot for interspersed directives
description:
Today one mid-document @prefix/@base after the body starts, or any SPARQL-style PREFIX/BASE keyword, drops the whole file to serial. Track running prefix/base state during the terminator pre-scan and emit per-chunk a snapshot of the prefix table as of that chunk's start. Acceptance: chunked == serial triple set on a fixture with interspersed @prefix + W3C TurtleTests; converts the 0x cliff to ~2x for tool-emitted/hand-written Turtle that redeclares mid-file.

Source: research/parsing-optimization-plan.md#T3
Notes: Source: parsing-optimization-plan.md Turtle T3 (Wave C3). Zero benefit for the common predicate-grouped Wikidata case; measurement-gated on target workloads. Subtle (the \# review-1398 bug). ready_now=false: gated on the rejection oracle (B4).

title: HDT: add zstd/bzip2 sniffing + zlib-ng backend for .hdt archives
description:
.hdt.gz is content-sniffed and streamed via MultiGzDecoder, but publishers also ship .hdt.zst / .hdt.bz2. Add zstd magic sniffing (0x28 B5 2F FD) + bzip2/xz, a flate2 zlib-ng backend (1.5-3x inflate), and remove the minor double-BufReader (lib.rs:93). Acceptance: decompress+parse of .hdt.gz/.hdt.zst/.hdt.bz2 yields a triple set identical to the plain load, benched via a new bench-hdt-zip entry.

Source: research/parsing-optimization-plan.md#H5
Notes: Sources: parsing-optimization-plan.md H5 (Wave B2). Compressed-HDT load is currently sniffed+streamed but unmeasured. Independent of H1/H3.

title: ZK: derivation_step module + entailmentRegime end-to-end
description:
Only EntailmentRegime::Simple is proved; no inference regime is tested. Add the derivation_step Noir module (one rule application: rule id + premise/conclusion hashes into the claim hash, rule semantics as a small in-circuit table per regime), a witness builder fed by sparq-reason's proof-trees ProofTree, and an obligation-compiler branch emitting one derivation_step per ProofNode. Acceptance: entailmentRegime: rdfs proven end-to-end over a proof-trees witness with the regime byte-bound into public inputs.

title: ZK: make filter_f64 manifest-composable for float-FILTER e2e
description:
filter_f64 is gate-counted and tested in isolation but is NOT manifest-composable — binding an f64 to a committed literal needs in-circuit float->canonical-decimal printing (unbudgeted), so there is zero float-FILTER end-to-end coverage in compose. Implement the in-circuit float->canonical-decimal encoding and wire FilterF64 into the manifest/binding edges. Acceptance: an xsd:double FILTER proven and verified end-to-end with f128 oracle vectors.
